title: Tech Note: Case-Sensitive Operations in 4th Dimension
author: David Adams
featured_technology: Script Manager / OS-dependent text comparison behavior

historical_commentary.text: This note addresses a core 4th Dimension 2004 language limitation — the engine's QUERY and string comparisons were natively case- and diacritic-insensitive — and provides workaround code for case-sensitive comparisons, especially motivated by the case-sensitivity requirements of XML element and attribute names in the era's growing web-services/XML integration work. Since then, 4D has added native case-sensitive comparison and search options directly to the classic language and query engine, reducing the need for the custom pointer-based comparison routines this note builds, though the underlying explanation of why case-sensitivity matters for XML remains accurate and useful context.
related_updates: 4D has since added native case-sensitive options to query, sort, and string comparison commands, reducing reliance on custom workaround code
4D's XML/JSON support has expanded considerably since 2005 with dedicated parsing and generation commands
